questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify scarcity in a resource-constrained sprint
questions.stem: A sprint has 40 developer hours but 60 hours of requested features. What does this gap illustrate?

options.text: Scarcity, because wants exceed the available developer hours
Surplus, because hours are left unused after delivery
options.misconception: assumes demand never exceeds available capacity

options.text: Inflation, because feature demand outpaces delivery speed
options.misconception: confuses price level rise with resource shortage

options.text: Efficiency, because every hour is fully productive
options.misconception: equates busy hours with absence of scarcity

questions.explanation: Scarcity arises when unlimited wants exceed finite resources. Here 60 requested hours exceed 40 available, so the gap is scarcity, not surplus or inflation.
questions.hint: Compare total wants to total available hours.

questions.explanation: Compound growth applies both factors. 50 times 1.10 times 1.10 equals 60.5 story points.
questions.hint: Apply the 10 percent factor twice.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain allocative efficiency in a ticket context
questions.stem: The team builds exactly what users value most with current resources. Explain why this is allocatively efficient.

answer.exemplar: Allocative efficiency holds because resources go to the highest-valued uses, matching user preferences.

questions.explanation: Allocative efficiency means resources are directed to uses with highest marginal benefit, matching preferences.
questions.hint: Connect resource use to user-valued outcomes.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute budget line slope
questions.stem: Licenses cost $250 and contractors cost $500. What is the budget line slope in licenses per contractor?
questions.explanation: Slope is the price ratio. 500 divided by 250 equals 2 licenses per contractor.
questions.hint: Divide contractor price by license price.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify the tradeoff between quality and speed
questions.stem: A ticket offers a quick fix now versus a thorough fix later. What tradeoff does this present?

options.text: No tradeoff, because both fix the bug
A sunk cost of prior code
options.misconception: confuses future choice with past spending

questions.explanation: The tradeoff is between quick immediate relief and durable quality. Choosing speed risks recurring issues.
questions.hint: Compare short-term relief to long-term durability.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute net present value of tooling
questions.stem: Tooling costs 8 hours now and saves 2 hours per sprint for 5 sprints. What is the net savings after 5 sprints?
questions.explanation: Gross savings are 2 times 5 equals 10 hours. Subtracting the 8 hour cost leaves 2 hours net saved.
questions.hint: Multiply per-sprint savings by sprints, then subtract cost.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain scarcity in a server capacity context
questions.stem: Server capacity handles 1000 requests but peak demand reaches 1500. Explain the scarcity problem this ticket reveals.

answer.exemplar: Scarcity exists because peak demand of 1500 requests exceeds the 1000 request server capacity.

questions.explanation: When demand exceeds capacity, scarcity forces prioritization or scaling. The gap is 500 requests.
questions.hint: Compare peak demand to available capacity.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute opportunity cost of a training sprint
questions.stem: A training sprint forgoes 3 features worth $2000 each. What is the opportunity cost of the training sprint?
questions.explanation: Three forgone features at $2000 each total $6000. That is the opportunity cost of training.
questions.hint: Multiply forgone features by their value.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain efficient production point
questions.stem: A team produces 4 features and 0 refactors, which is the maximum features possible. What does this point represent?

options.misconception: confuses output level with resource shortage

options.text: An efficient point on the frontier

questions.explanation: Producing maximum features with given resources is an efficient point on the production possibilities frontier.
questions.hint: Check whether output is maximized for the resource level.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain growth from process improvement
questions.stem: A team adopts a new deployment pipeline that cuts release time in half. Explain how this affects economic growth.

answer.exemplar: The pipeline improvement is technological progress, which shifts the production possibilities frontier outward and raises growth.

questions.explanation: Technological progress expands productive capacity without more resources, driving economic growth and an outward frontier shift.
questions.hint: Relate process improvement to capacity expansion.
